topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, administrative context, and overview comparison for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Complement system overview, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of the complement system, its naming conventions, and the central biochemical role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that initiate complement and drive local C3 deposition past the activation threshold.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the primary immunological outcomes following complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation and protection against complement attack
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how host cells utilize surface and soluble regulatory proteins to inhibit inappropriate complement activation on self-tissues.

topics.label: Clinical pathology of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical manifestations and disease vulnerabilities associated with genetic and acquired complement component deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and biomedical applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how microorganisms circumvent complement-mediated destruction and highlights clinical and laboratory uses of microbial evasion proteins.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture closing and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
